title: Plugin batch 2: agent routing and follow-ups
objective: Second plugin batch: agent routing by model strength plus model fallback, work state in the repo, robust run-all, gate multi-wave fix, pipeline follow-ups.

tasks.objective: Agent routing by model strength and model fallback, per the approved routing plan (each model takes the kinds it is strong at; changes: registry routing, fallback, plan fields, one route() helper, docs and tests). Registry pipeline.agent_routing (kind -> agent: code/test/fix/refactor/generated -> codex; docs/policy/design/lead -> claude), pipeline.qa_prefer codex, pipeline.available_agents + env RPG_FACTORY_AGENTS fallback with a SAME_MODEL (fallback: X unavailable) marker the gate accepts; optional kind and reason on plan tasks and subtasks; one route() helper replaces every default_implementer read; validate/subplan validate WARN on unexplained overrides and on one-model plans; QA model choice; parallel-work.md section 10 'Which model' table (single copy) and the token rule (Claude leads and plans, Codex implements code and runs long QA); SKILL.md and AGENTS.md pointers; tests and changelog fragment. Dogfood the rule in the subplan: code subtask implemented by codex, docs subtask by claude, placement shared. Availability must never stop a task: detect available agents automatically (each pipeline.agents.<a>.bin on PATH, plus the Orca agent list when Orca runs; env RPG_FACTORY_AGENTS overrides; a runtime MODEL_UNAVAILABLE such as a revoked token or 401 marks the model down for the run). With only claude on the machine every role (implement, review, QA, lead) routes to claude; with only codex every role routes to codex, including the task lead; reviews then carry SAME_MODEL (fallback: <model> unavailable) and the gate accepts them. dispatch and status print which model each role got and why; no command errors because a model is missing.

tasks.objective: QA tiers: stop re-running the full suite. Follow the run lead's approved QA-tiers plan (sections 'Tiers' and 'Changes' 1-6, 'Subtasks'). (1) tests/run-all.sh: one full run per machine via a lock in the persistent state dir (wait / --no-wait exit 3 / stale takeover), a result record per clean tree and --reuse that exits 0 at once on a PASS record of the same tree. (2) tests/affected.py: scripts/lib/* no longer GLOBAL; map lib modules to their importers statically, unsure means run; tests/affected.test.sh. (3) tests/git-guard.test.sh batch mode through scripts/git-guard.py --batch (same evaluate path), ~30 cases keep the real hook process; same case count, record wall time before and after. (4) registry pipeline.qa_tiers {task: affected, integration: full}; dispatch --phase qa names the tier command (task: --affected --base <review base> -j 2, never a full run; integration: --reuse -j 4 under the lock; re-QA: failed suites + --affected from the previous candidate); validate WARNs on a full run in task checks or acceptance. (5) claude docs: QA tiers table in parallel-work.md section 10 (single copy, mutation test), .claude/CLAUDE.md PR rule, Commands (--reuse, --no-wait) and Operating lessons (one full run per machine), changelog fragment. Subtasks: runall-lock-reuse, affected-narrow, guard-batch, pipeline-qa-tier (codex), policy-docs (claude); placement shared. This task's own QA uses the new tier: --affected, never a full run. (6) docs/plans: sync docs/plans/plugin-flow-2.json with the run lead's live plan (repo path stays ../..) and drop full runs from the task checks of the next tasks in docs/plans/backlog.md (claude, part of policy-docs). (7) Speed, measured at 09ef888 (sum of suite times 4973 s): parallel-policy 831 s, git-guard 717 s, routing 393 s, pipeline 312 s, facts 225 s, run-checks 212 s. (a) Suite-level reuse: run-all records per suite a PASS keyed by a hash of the suite's inputs (the suite file + the files affected.py maps to it + GLOBAL inputs + tool versions); a later run (task re-QA or the integration full run) skips a suite whose input hash already PASSED and prints `reused <suite> (inputs <hash>)`; `--no-reuse` forces; unsure mapping means run. (b) tests/parallel-policy.test.sh: build the throwaway copy once and run each mutation's lint only on the mutated file's checks (or in parallel), target under 120 s. (c) tests/routing.test.sh history replay: cache replay results keyed by commit SHA + registry hash; replay only new commits. (d) run-all prepends the real Python directory (sys.executable of python3 -c) to PATH for the suites when python3 resolves to the Windows Store alias (about 70 ms per call; no change to the user's system). (e) tests/pipeline.test.sh: build fixture git repos once and copy them per case instead of re-creating. Record before/after wall times per suite. Subtasks: suite-reuse (codex, tests/run-all.sh with runall-lock-reuse, so one subtask), policy-speed (codex), routing-cache (codex), pipeline-fixtures (codex, with pipeline-qa-tier). Targets: task QA under 10 min including the session; integration full run under 10 min when most suites reuse. (8) User rule 2026-11-08: a task never runs the whole suite. Task QA = exactly the suites of the task's own change: the task `checks` plus the suites tests/affected.py maps to the changed files (narrowed per item 2), each suite once (a check that names a suite already selected is not run twice; suite reuse skips unchanged inputs). dispatch --phase qa prints that one command (`tests/run-all.sh --only-suites <list>` or `--affected --base <review base>` deduplicated with the checks) and the spec forbids a full run. Small tasks (tier S, or every changed path docs/skills/changelog): no separate QA session - the task lead runs the same command after the review PASS and records `verdict --phase qa --by <lead> --note 'tier S: lead ran task suites'`; the gate accepts it for tier S only. The only full run is integration, once per batch, with suite reuse.
